methodology: US federal withholding on lottery/gambling winnings for non-resident aliens is a flat 30% (IRC §871(a)). effective_total_tax_pct_at_500m_usd is the combined US + home-country effective rate computed by ChamTax’s calculation engine for a $500,000,000 lump-sum payout (chosen because it is large enough that every country’s top-bracket/flat-rate approximation applies), after any Foreign Tax Credit the country’s law/treaty allows. confidence: "verified" = primary statute/treaty/official guidance found; "approximate" = reasonable secondary-source estimate, some structural simplification; "estimate" = best-effort, no authoritative primary source found — see chamtax.com’s per-country landing pages for full citations.
unit: percent (except country_code, country_name, tax_authority, confidence, tax_structure_notes)

rows.name: South Korea
rows.structure: Progressive (comprehensive income tax, 8 brackets up to 45%) + 10% local surtax, FTC applied

rows.name: Pakistan
rows.structure: ⚠️ Base 35% + 8% super tax + 10% surcharge on the base; FTC offsets only the base-rate component, not super tax/surcharge

rows.name: China
rows.structure: Flat 20% "incidental income" tax, FTC applied

rows.name: India
rows.structure: Flat 30% + 25% surcharge + 4% cess (≈39% effective), no deductions, FTC applied

rows.name: Vietnam
rows.structure: Flat 10% prize-income tax, FTC applied under domestic law (no US-Vietnam treaty in force)

rows.name: Indonesia
rows.structure: Flat 25% final tax on lottery winnings, no FTC (domestic final-tax credit procedure under Art. 24 excludes this Art. 4(2) final-tax category; treaty-based relief unconfirmed) — stacks in full on top of US withholding

rows.name: Philippines
rows.structure: Approximated at the top progressive bracket (35%) since foreign winnings do not get the 20% domestic-lottery final tax rate; FTC applied

rows.name: Thailand
rows.authority: Estimate based on Revenue Department data/IRS
rows.structure: ⚠️ No clear official guidance found for foreign lottery winnings; approximated at the top personal income tax bracket (35%)

rows.name: Japan
rows.structure: "Temporary income" with 1/2 inclusion, taxed at top marginal rate (≈27.97% effective), FTC applied

rows.name: Russia
rows.structure: Flat top progressive rate (22%); FTC believed unavailable since the US-Russia tax treaty’s double-taxation article has been suspended since 2023

rows.name: Nepal
rows.structure: Flat 25% "windfall gain" final tax, FTC applied under domestic law

rows.name: Sri Lanka
rows.structure: Approximated at the top progressive bracket (36%); a possible 15% preferential rate for remitted foreign income has unclear applicability to lottery winnings

rows.name: Uzbekistan
rows.structure: Flat 12% on all personal income, no FTC (US-Uzbekistan relations still run on the 1973 US-USSR treaty, with no general "other income" or double-tax-relief article covering lottery winnings) — stacks in full on top of US withholding

rows.name: Kazakhstan
rows.structure: Flat 10% on "winnings"-category income, FTC applied

rows.name: Kyrgyzstan
rows.structure: Flat 10% on personal income including winnings, no FTC (same 1973 US-USSR treaty as Uzbekistan, no general foreign-tax-credit article; no unilateral domestic relief found) — stacks in full on top of US withholding

rows.name: Myanmar
rows.structure: Approximated at the top bracket (25%) for "income from other sources", no FTC (no US-Myanmar tax treaty in force) — stacks in full on top of US withholding

rows.name: Bangladesh
rows.structure: Flat 25% on "income from other sources" (prizes), FTC applied

rows.name: Cambodia
rows.structure: ⚠️ No clear legal basis found for taxing personal lottery/prize income — treated as 0% pending verification, NOT a confirmed exemption

rows.name: Mongolia
rows.authority: Estimate based on Tax Administration data/IRS
rows.structure: ⚠️ Approximated at 40% per secondary-source summaries; not independently verified against primary legislation

rows.name: Laos
rows.authority: Estimate based on Ministry of Finance data/IRS
rows.structure: ⚠️ Flat 5% under the new income tax law; no US-Laos tax treaty, so no FTC — stacks fully on top of US withholding

rows.name: Canada
rows.structure: Non-taxable windfall under the Income Tax Act — no domestic tax base

rows.name: Taiwan
rows.structure: Worldwide-income Alternative Minimum Tax, flat 20% on foreign-source income above NT$7.5M, FTC applied against the AMT increase

rows.name: Hong Kong
rows.structure: Territorial system (salaries/profits/property tax only) — lottery winnings fall outside all three, no domestic tax base

rows.name: United Kingdom
rows.structure: No Income Tax, Capital Gains Tax, or National Insurance on gambling/lottery winnings — no domestic tax base

rows.name: Australia
rows.structure: Non-assessable windfall gain, not income — no domestic tax base

rows.name: Mexico
rows.structure: Foreign winnings taxed as "other income" at the top progressive bracket (35%), FTC applied

rows.name: France
rows.structure: Pure games of chance fall outside taxable-income categories under the CGI — no domestic tax base

rows.name: New Zealand
rows.structure: Non-taxable windfall, not assessable income — no domestic tax base

rows.name: Ireland
rows.structure: Betting/lottery/prize winnings have never been within any taxable-income category — no domestic tax base

rows.name: Singapore
rows.structure: Official IRAS FAQ: gambling/lottery winnings are windfall, not taxable income — no domestic tax base

rows.name: South Africa
rows.structure: Capital in nature, excluded from "gross income" and exempt from CGT — no domestic tax base

rows.name: Malaysia
rows.structure: Non-taxable windfall under the Income Tax Act 1967 — no domestic tax base

rows.name: Germany
rows.structure: Falls outside all 7 enumerated taxable-income categories (EStG) — "nicht steuerbar", no domestic tax base

rows.name: Netherlands
rows.structure: ⚠️ Kansspelbelasting (games-of-chance tax), flat 37.8% — a separate tax head with no FTC provision found, stacks in full on top of US withholding

rows.name: Sweden
rows.structure: Flat 30% capital-income tax on non-EU/EEA winnings; FTC exactly offsets the 30% US withholding (coincidence of equal rates)

rows.name: Norway
rows.structure: Flat 22% general-income rate; FTC fully absorbs the (lower) Norwegian tax, residual 0

rows.name: Denmark
rows.structure: Top marginal personal-income rate (57.07%, incl. 2026 "top-top tax"); FTC leaves the largest residual of any supported country (≈27pp)

rows.name: Finland
rows.structure: Top marginal rate (46.17%) on non-EEA winnings; FTC leaves a residual of ≈16pp

rows.name: Italy
rows.structure: Top progressive IRPEF bracket + regional/municipal surtax (≈47.23% combined); FTC leaves a residual of ≈17pp

rows.name: Poland
rows.structure: General progressive tax (12%/32%) + 4% solidarity levy above PLN 1M, approximated at 36% combined; FTC leaves a residual of ≈6pp

rows.name: Turkey
rows.structure: ⚠️ Taxed under inheritance/transfer tax law (VİVK), flat 20%, not income tax — outside the income tax treaty’s scope, no FTC, stacks in full
